plain_summary: The Wu Lab builds open-source software infrastructure that makes scattered biomedical data findable, accessible, and reusable (FAIR) for researchers everywhere. Its flagship BioThings suite — MyGene.info, MyVariant.info, MyChem.info, MyDisease.info, MyTaxon.info, and MyGeneset.info — are high-performance web APIs giving instant, standardized access to integrated knowledge on genes, genetic variants, chemicals/drugs, diseases, taxonomy, and gene sets, together handling over 30 million requests a month. Behind these sits the BioThings SDK, an open-source Python toolkit the lab built so anyone can create their own self-updating biomedical API. BioGPS offers a friendlier, web-based gene portal for exploring annotations alongside genomic datasets. The Data Discovery Engine helps research institutions register datasets under FAIR-aligned metadata schemas so they're searchable by tools like Google and specialized portals such as the NIAID Data Ecosystem. BioThings Explorer, paired with the SmartAPI registry, queries many distributed biomedical databases at once, serving as core infrastructure for the NCATS Biomedical Data Translator program used in precision medicine and drug repurposing. Outbreak.info supported SARS-CoV-2 variant surveillance. Together, these tools matter because biomedical knowledge is fragmented across countless incompatible databases — the Wu Lab's infrastructure stitches it together so discoveries happen faster.
trajectory: The lab is expanding its federated knowledge-graph infrastructure: BioThings Explorer and the SmartAPI registry already connect dozens of Translator Knowledge Provider APIs (62 and counting) built on the BioThings SDK, with the lab stating it will keep adding new knowledge sources as they're identified. It is also extending the Data Discovery Engine's schema-driven approach into new domain-specific portals like the NIAID Data Ecosystem, and continuing to scale its core BioThings APIs (MyGene.info, MyVariant.info, MyChem.info, MyDisease.info), which already serve tens of thousands of users and tens of millions of requests monthly.
